problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(0,-1),(1,1),$ and $(3,2).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the action of $T?$

- $(-1,4)$
- $(-2,4)$
- $(1,-3)$

Consider the linear transformation $\mathbf T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062587/assets/3ff8dc37a532cfe49a2fbd8c02a1b27c50642d8e4c54def6984f3596f68065fa.png)

A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(-1,2), (0,1)$ and $(1,1).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of $S',$ the image of $S$ under the action of $\mathbf T?$

- $(-2,0)$

- $(0,0)$

- $(2,0)$
examples.worked_solution:
To find the image of $S$ under the action of $\mathbf T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S\mathbin{:}$

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under $\mathbf T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of $S'$ are $(-2,0),$ $(0,0),$ and $(2,0).$

So, the correct answer is "I, II,  and III."
